entities.summary: Minden Cathedral, dedicated to Saints Gorgonius and Peter, is a Roman Catholic church in the city of Minden, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. From the year 803 AD, when the area was conquered by Charlemagne, Minden was the center of a diocese and subsequently became the center of a small sovereign state, a prince-bishopric (Hochstift) of Minden, until the time of the Peace of Westphalia (1648), when Minden was secularized as the Principality of Minden. Despite the whole principality became a protestant region, the cathedral remained Catholic, and the Cathedral chapter consisted of Catholic and Protestant members until it was abolished in 1810.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Minden Cathedral played a significant role in the region of Western Europe during the Middle Ages, serving as the center of a diocese and later a prince-bishopric. Its enduring Catholic presence despite the surrounding region's conversion to Protestantism had lasting implications for the local power dynamics.
